scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PCs in the IT Department (192.168.1.x) report they cannot reach
their gateway (192.168.1.1) or anything off-subnet. CS Dept PCs
(192.168.2.x) and all other zones are unaffected. Identify the
failure.

injection.action: bring down the bridge that carries IT Dept LAN

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show br0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: switch0 br0 (L2 fabric for IT Dept LAN)
Mechanism: switch0's br0 carries the IT Dept LAN's path to
  router0's 192.168.1.1 SVI. With br0 down, IT hosts lose their
  gateway and all off-subnet reachability. Other subnets are on
  different switches/bridges, so they're unaffected.
Localization: switch0
Root cause: br0 administratively down on switch0
Fix: `ip link set br0 up` on switch0
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set br0 up` on switch0

line.command: ip -br link show br0 | grep -c UP

agent.diagnosis_text:
The IT Department (192.168.1.x) is completely isolated from its gateway (router0 eth0 at 192.168.1.1) due to the Linux bridge `br0` on switch0 being administratively shut down. Switch0 is the sole Layer 2 path between the IT LAN segment (`lan_it`) and router0's eth0 (`link_r0_sw0`); with `br0` down, no Ethernet frames can traverse it in either direction.

**Mechanism:** When `ip link set br0 down` is issued on a Linux bridge, the kernel immediately moves all bridge member ports into the STP "disabled" state, halting all forwarding. This is exactly what dmesg records on switch0 — after an initial healthy STP convergence (both ports reached "forwarding" state), both eth0 and eth1 simultaneously entered "disabled" state within 17 µs of each other at kernel time ~164466 s, the hallmark of an administrative `br0 down` event. Since no L2 frames can reach router0's eth0, ARP requests from IT hosts never get a reply, and every host in the IT segment receives "Destination Host Unreachable" for the gateway and all off-subnet destinations.

**Localization:** switch0, bridge interface `br0`. Both member ports (eth0 = link to router0, eth1 = IT LAN) are in STP "disabled" state; `br0` state is DOWN. The startup script correctly includes `ip link set dev br0 up`, confirming this was a post-startup fault injection and not a configuration error.

**Root cause:** `br0` on switch0 was explicitly brought down after lab startup (via `ip link set br0 down`), dropping the entire IT segment off the network.

**Corrective fix:** Run `ip link set br0 up` on switch0. The STP timers will restart, ports will pass through learning → forwarding (completing in ~30 s with default STP settings), and IT Department connectivity will be fully restored.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly localizes the failure to switch0 (bridge br0 and its member ports).
The report explicitly identifies the affected component as switch0's Linux bridge br0 (the switch fabric).
The diagnosis explicitly localizes the failure to switch0's br0 and describes loss of gateway reachability only for the IT (192.168.1.x) segment, distinguishing that scope from other subnets.
Proposes the exact corrective action—bringing br0 up on switch0 (ip link set br0 up)—which matches the expected fix.

The agent's logs show br0 on switch0 is administratively DOWN, dmesg records the bridge ports moving from forwarding to disabled simultaneously, and the startup script shows br0 was brought up at boot — together these observations justify the conclusion that br0 was later brought down and caused the outage. Evidence is present for the key claims and the inferred cause is a logical explanation of the observed kernel events and connectivity symptoms.
